liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls this one of the hottest Truckins ever played, with energy staying high all night; Reviewer finds the Truckin' very powerful, with Jerry flying on nearly every tune [6][7][9]
- **Cassidy** (2 reviews): Reviewer hears Cassidy as the first sign the band was on form this night; First-set Cassidy singled out as awesome, showing outstanding playing [8][9]
- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Weir flubs part of a line but recovers; Jerry's jam picks up near the four-minute mark, and drummers fill the beats before the final verse; The small skip out of the jam before the last verse is praised as a moment of turning water into wine [8][10]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Jerry's solo is somewhat extended compared with the usually short 1977-78 versions; Estimated-Eyes is praised for spirited Garcia playing [11][14]
- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer calls Deal a rock and roll version that gives you your money's worth [8]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): The transition into Eyes is nice, though Bobby rushes it slightly [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Take a Step Back #1**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [18]
- **Take a Step Back #2**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [18]
- **Take a Step Back #3**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-11-21.sbd.carpenter-andrewf.87023.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 27 songs; 182 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is described as solid; The soundboard has many gaps and cuts, filled with ShnID-11667 audience patches, including all of Stagger Lee, Drums and Johnny B. Goode [1][14]
- **gd1978-11-21.176596.aud.Maddex.vernon.andrewf.flac1648**: audience recording; 23 songs; 173 min [2]
- **gd78-11-21.aud.wiley.11667.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 165 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is described as okay, and the reviewer wishes soundboards were available; Reviewer says the audience recording is lacking, despite the show itself being top-notch; Audience recording is called okay; the soundboard versions are rough with many patches [6][7][11]
- **gd1978-11-21.sbd-part.unknown.30116.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 16 songs; 92 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard portion is missing from Stagger Lee onward, so the audience recording supplies the remainder, including crowd noise track [4]

## Around the show

- Arriving late from Cleveland the night before, the reviewer found the old hockey arena's glass doors hanging off hinges and no ticket takers [7]
- Reviewer drove with friends from Buffalo; describes the Rochester auditorium as unassuming, with an energetic band and crowd [9]
- Reviewer came from school in Albany, met college friends on the arena floor, described the venue as tiny, and slept at the Greyhound station [12]
- A Rochester native who studied in Binghamton came home for the show and enjoyed the floor [13]
- Reviewer calls it part of an underrated November 1978 tour [14]
- Reviewer counted about 39 repetitions of the 'don't let that deal go down' line, versus about 47 in the Nashville version [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-11-21.sbd.carpenter-andrewf.87023.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Ted Carpenter and Andrew F; source: SBD > ? > Cassettes provided by Ted Carpenter. [1]
- **gd1978-11-21.176596.aud.Maddex.vernon.andrewf.flac1648**: taped by Lee Maddex collection.; transferred by Matt Vernon & AndrewF; source: AUD (unknown gear & lineage) via the Lee Maddex collection. [2]. Also: Maddex audience recording, a complete show not matching current sources as of March 2026, with ID-11667 patches in Bertha, Stagger Lee and Drums [2]
- **gd78-11-21.aud.wiley.11667.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [3]. Also: Audience source lineage is AUD to MC to DAT to CDR, seeded to Etree by T. Wiley [3]
- **gd1978-11-21.sbd-part.unknown.30116.sbeok.flac16**: source: SBD > ? > Cassette [4]. Also: Partial soundboard is an unlineaged cassette, patched with audience source from the archive from Stagger Lee onward [4]
